display.title: The Caliph's Secretary
display.summary_short: Captured by pirates and sold as a slave in Baghdad, young Dina, daughter of Chacham Nissim, becomes secretary to the Caliph while her father, disguised as a beggar, tries to free her.
display.summary_long: Chacham Nissim, leader of the Jews of Alexandria, and his daughter Dina are seized by pirates on their way to Spain and brought to the slave market of Baghdad in the days of the Caliph al-Mamun. The Jewish community of nearby Samarra, led by the Rav, Mar Yaakov, and the court doctor Hakim Isaac, refuses to pay the slave trader's ransom, and before dawn a powerful courtier, Al-Kisai, carries Dina off. Her father escapes by leaping into the river and hides in Mar Yaakov's house. Dina, thirteen and motherless, is taken in by Al-Kisai's kind wife, who tells her to hide that she is Jewish. Her brilliant letters make her Al-Kisai's 'little secretary' and then the Caliph's own. Her father sits outside the palace gate dressed as a beggar, and the two exchange secret signs. When Al-Kisai persuades the Caliph to expel all the Jews, Dina sees why Hashem placed her in the palace, like Esther. A rescue plan is betrayed by a kitchen slave, the Jewish leaders are arrested, and everything comes down to a dramatic trial before the Caliph, where Dina and her father refuse to give up their faith.
display.lesson: Hashem guides every step with hashgachah pratis, and a Jew stays loyal to Yiddishkeit even at the risk of his life. Kindness and courage can change even an enemy's heart.

advisories.note: Jewish captives are sold as slaves and a thirteen-year-old girl is torn from her father; she is treated kindly.
A courtier wins a decree expelling all Jews; the community leaders are chained and imprisoned.
Father and daughter are told to convert or die; they refuse.
A fight on the slave ship and an order to whip the father at the trial.
Dina's mother and the courtier's only daughter have passed away (mentioned).

characters: Mar Yaakov, the Rav of Samarra

segments.title: The slave ship in Baghdad
segments.summary: The Jews of Samarra cannot pay the slave trader's price, and Dina is carried off by an important stranger while a man leaps into the river.

segments.title: Chacham Nissim's escape
segments.summary: After a 'next part' break, Chacham Nissim appears at Mar Yaakov's door and tells how he escaped from the ship.

segments.title: Dina in Al-Kisai's house
segments.summary: A kind woman takes Dina in, and her wisdom and handwriting make her Al-Kisai's little secretary.

segments.title: The beggar at the gate
segments.summary: Disguised as a beggar, Chacham Nissim finds his daughter, and she sends him her mother's kerchief as a sign.

segments.title: Secretary to the Caliph and the evil decree
segments.summary: Dina is called to the Caliph's palace just as Al-Kisai wins a decree expelling the Jews, and the Caliph secretly asks the Jews for a plan.

segments.title: The escape plan and the arrest
segments.summary: Chacham Nissim's rescue plan is betrayed and the Jewish leaders are put in chains.

segments.title: The trial before the Caliph
segments.summary: Dina shields her father, refuses to give up her faith, and an unexpected voice changes the outcome for all the Jews.

quality.notes: Complete telling (about 103 min) of a story that was told in parts; a 'listen in to the next part' break at 20:11. Opens directly with the story, no theme song. ASR spells the courtier variously (Alkisei, Al-Qisay) and the Rav 'Mariakob'.

needs_human_review: Narrator attributed to the weekly storyteller by style only (no theme song, no name, no sign-off); series left null.
Possibly earlier Chacham Nissim stories exist (opens with the flight from Alexandria).
